correctness.rationale: For odd p not dividing Q, the ratio a/b lies in F_p^*, so its order h divides p-1. If h is even, writing h=2r gives exactly the odd multiples of r as p-divisible indices, and LTE gives nu_p(V_{rk})=e+nu_p(k) for odd k. The prime-power Dold criterion then follows because every support-changing q-power divides h and therefore p-1. For p=2, coprimality reduces to opposite parity or odd-odd; the latter has p-part 2^c on odd indices and 2 on even indices, whose only nonzero Möbius transforms are at 1 and 2. The realizability obstruction is the explicit negative transform 1-p^e at 2r, or 2-2^c at p=2. The standalone exact checker confirms 1700 finite cases through n=120.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly leaves extension to general V(P,Q) and U(P,Q) as an open direction. The 2021 survey covers the global Dold property of trace sequences but not local p-parts, and the recent classical Lucas result itself shows that global trace-Dold does not force local Dold. published-finding corpus and web searches returned no statement covering the all-prime local Dold classification for the split square-discriminant companion branch.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural structural branch of an explicit recent open direction: for every coprime split companion Lucas sequence it gives the complete local Dold-prime set (all primes) and an exact realizability criterion. The result explains why split characteristic roots eliminate the local Dold failures seen in the classical nonsplit Lucas sequence, via the decisive order-divides-p-1 mechanism.
